constraint: must fit the chosen wall with its open footprint and a walking clearance
notes: «Bigger the better. Standard sizes are 1400, 1600 and 1800. If it's possible to place 1800, it's better to place 1800.» !! SO THE MODEL PICKS: largest option that fits each candidate wall, and the answer may differ per candidate - which is itself the comparison worth seeing.

constraint: vertical needs cabinet HEIGHT ~ mattress length + mechanism + plinth; horizontal needs wall LENGTH ~ mattress length
notes: «Most wall beds are vertical... it doesn't make a significant difference for us; probably vertical is the most common design.» !! A WEAK preference, so it may be traded for fit. The real difference is which dimension it spends: vertical spends ceiling height, horizontal spends wall length. With 2500 mm clear height, vertical is comfortable for a 2000 mm mattress; horizontal would need ~2000 mm of uninterrupted wall instead.

constraint: sets the wall-bed CABINET DEPTH, which is taken out of the room's floor depth
notes: «Depends on the construction of the bed. Of course we would like a thicker mattress, for comfort. The thicker the better.» ⚠️⚠️ AND THIS ONE FIGHTS ITSELF - see PAR-MATTRESS-CONFLICT in the notes column of the envelope record. No standard option list is given because the bed's own mechanism constrains it; it is the manufacturer's number, not a free choice.
Standard is 600 and smaller is a special-situation exception. Treated as near-constant rather than a preference to maximise: deeper than 600 buys nothing, since 600 is what a coat hanger needs.

constraint: the parked stack must have somewhere to go that is not a doorway, a radiator or a window reveal
notes: Four or five leaves, glass, fully retractable. More leaves means a shorter parked stack per leaf but more hardware; the owner has not expressed a preference between them, so the model should report the parked depth for BOTH.

constraint: concrete takes the load directly; aerated block needs EITHER chemical anchors OR a floor-bearing support frame
notes: !!⚠️ THIS CONSTRAINS WHICH WALL CAN HOST THE BED, and the vault already carries it. The maker (Freedom, YT_qMGSfO-glvc) states it directly: «надёжное крепление кровати возможно ТОЛЬКО К БЕТОННОЙ СТЕНЕ. Для других стен существует опорная рама. Она распределяет нагрузку НА ПОЛ.» !! THE CRITERION IS THE MATERIAL, NOT THE STRUCTURAL ROLE - the vault corrected its own 'load-bearing' paraphrase on 2026-09-15. A load-bearing block wall is still not concrete. A second maker allows aerated block with CHEMICAL anchors, six-point fixing - four angle brackets high, two concealed low - «они держат в любой поверхности». So block is workable, but ONLY with the fixing specified in ADVANCE, which makes this a rough-stage decision rather than a joinery one. !! CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LAYOUT: the R-series concrete walls are the unconditional candidates; a G-series block wall costs either chemical anchors or a support frame that eats floor depth.
